words.gloss: to the people of the world

literal: Blame, they say, to all the people of the world, if they do not obtain the legacy called fame.
translation: For all people living on this earth, it is said to be a disgrace if they fail to acquire the lasting legacy called fame.
modern: உலகில் வாழும் மக்கள் அனைவருக்கும், புகழ் என்று சொல்லப்படும் எஞ்சி நிற்கும் அழியாத செல்வத்தைப் பெறாவிட்டால், அதுவே பழி என்று கூறுவர்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme importance of earning a good reputation during one's lifetime. The word 'icai' means fame, and 'eaccam' refers to a legacy or that which remains after one is gone. The poet states that if a person does not acquire this lasting legacy of fame, their life is considered a 'vacai', meaning a disgrace or blame. Thus, living a life that leaves no honorable memory behind is deemed a failure by the world.
